input.quote: 28.1 This Agreement is governed exclusively by Singapore law, and the courts of Singapore have exclusive jurisdiction.
input.rationale: Section 28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts — Vendor-side territory outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales) and walk-away for us. It also directly conflicts with § 28.2, which already grants the state and federal courts in New York County exclusive jurisdiction with only a temporary injunctive relief carve-out (that carve-out does not defeat the exclusive merits forum, and the § 28.3 escalation is acceptable). The shortest cure is to change the governing law in § 28.1 to New York and drop the conflicting Singapore forum words, so the forum element already satisfied by § 28.2 stands unaltered.

mappings.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
mappings.quote: The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction, and each Party irrevocably submits to personal jurisdiction and waives any objection based on venue or inconvenient forum. Nothing prevents a Party from seeking temporary injunctive relief in another court with jurisdiction to protect confidential information or intellectual property.

proposal.summary: Change governing law in § 28.1 from Singapore to New York and delete the conflicting Singapore exclusive-jurisdiction wording, leaving § 28.2's New York County forum intact.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We moved governing law to New York, which is our accepted position, and removed the Singapore exclusive-jurisdiction wording because it conflicts with the New York County forum already agreed in § 28.2. Delaware, California, or England and Wales law with the corresponding courts would also work for us.
